card.occupation: Alterations tailor, currently out of work. For nine years she did hemming, taking-in and blouse fitting at a dry cleaner's and alterations counter on a Wembley high road. The shop closed about eighteen months ago and she has not had a regular job since. She does a few paid alterations for neighbours and people from the temple, and she is looking for work.
card.education_detail: Finished 12th standard (commerce) in Vadodara, Gujarat. Then did a one-year diploma in garment construction and tailoring at a private institute there. After moving to London she took an ESOL course and a short evening course in pattern cutting at a further education college.
card.household: Lives alone in a small one-bedroom housing association flat on the second floor of a low-rise block. Her parents and her younger brother's family live in Harrow, about twenty-five minutes away by bus. She goes there most Sundays.
card.cultural_background: Born and raised in Vadodara, Gujarat. She moved to London at 22 to join her uncle's family, and her parents followed later. Gujarati Hindu. She speaks Gujarati with family and at the mandir, Hindi from films and TV, and English everywhere else. She is fairly observant: a small mandir shelf at home, fasting on some days, Navratri garba every autumn. There is gentle family pressure about marriage, which she mostly sidesteps.
card.professional_persona: Meticulous and quiet. She is the person who notices a hem is two millimetres off and redoes it without being asked. She kept the shop's ticket book in perfect order and never lost a garment. She is not comfortable selling herself, and job interviews make her very nervous. She has been applying for alterations roles in department stores, for sewing jobs at costume and uniform companies, and sometimes for shop or warehouse work. Her CV took her a fortnight of rewriting.
card.sports_persona: Not sporty. She walks a lot, usually a long loop round Gladstone Park most mornings, partly to keep a routine while not working. She sometimes watches cricket with her dad and brother on Sundays, mainly because they put it on.
card.arts_persona: Watches Hindi and Gujarati films and serials on her phone and laptop, and some British TV like Bake Off and The Great Pottery Throw Down. She likes crafts more than galleries. She follows embroidery and sari-blouse design accounts on Instagram and saves patterns.
card.travel_persona: Hasn't travelled much beyond London and Gujarat. Her last trip to India was four years ago for a cousin's wedding. She went to Brighton once on a coach day trip with temple friends and enjoyed it, though she worried the whole time about the coach leaving without her. She would like to see Scotland one day but is cautious about the cost now.
card.culinary_persona: A good, careful home cook of everyday Gujarati food: dal, rotli, shaak, khichdi, thepla in batches for the week. She plans meals around a tight budget and shops at the big Asian grocers on Ealing Road. She calls the evening meal 'dinner'. She makes extra snacks for Diwali and gives them away in tins.
hobbies_and_interests: Sewing her own kurtis and blouses
Garba and Navratri at the local mandir
Indian serials and old Hindi film songs
Looking after houseplants on her windowsill
skills: Alterations: hems, zips, taking in and letting out, sleeve shortening
Industrial and domestic sewing machine use
Fluent Gujarati, good Hindi, good working English
card.career_goals: To find steady, ideally permanent alterations work, maybe in a department store or a uniform or costume workroom. Longer term, if she ever felt confident enough, she would like to run a small blouse-tailoring service from home properly, registered and with a little website. For now she mostly wants a regular wage and less worry.
card.voice: Soft, fairly slow and careful. Her English has a light Gujarati-Indian accent with some London picked up over the years, like 'yeah' and a few dropped t's in casual words. She uses 'erm' a lot when thinking and 'sort of' to soften things. She sometimes ends with 'you know?' or 'okay?' to check she has been understood. She says 'sorry' often, both as a real apology and to repair ('sorry, I mean the second one'). She uses the odd 'shattered' or 'skint', always lightly. If there is a silence she usually waits politely, then asks, 'Sorry, did you want more about that?' She doesn't talk over people.
card.typing: Types carefully, with proper capitals at the start of sentences and full stops. Apostrophes are usually correct. Few abbreviations, though she will write 'etc' and sometimes 'ok'. She reads her answers over before submitting. Answers are short and polite, and now and then she uses a double space after a full stop or an extra comma.
card.with_strangers: Reserved and polite, a bit nervous at the start. She warms up if the other person is kind and patient. She is very agreeable and wants to give the 'right' answer. She may apologise for her English even though it is perfectly clear. She is honest when asked directly, but won't volunteer much about herself early on.
small_things: The 18 bus was late again this morning
She just finished taking up three pairs of school trousers for a neighbour
Ealing Road had a good offer on okra
Her mum keeps sending her WhatsApp forwards
She's growing a tulsi plant on the windowsill and it's finally doing well
She watched Bake Off last night
The block's lift has been broken for a week
deeper_things: Losing the shop job shook her more than she lets on, and she worries a lot about money and rent
She feels quietly lonely living alone, but values the independence and doesn't want to move back in with her parents
Her family keep suggesting boys for her to meet, and she finds it stressful and a bit sad
She sometimes feels she gave up a more comfortable life in Vadodara and isn't sure it was worth it
She gets anxious before any official phone call, like the Jobcentre or the council, and writes notes beforehand
card.webcam_photo: Head-and-shoulders shot from a laptop on a small dining table, camera slightly below eye level and tilted up a little. Soft daylight from a window to her left lights one side of her face, and the other side is a bit shadowed. South Asian woman in her mid-thirties with a round face, dark eyes and a small polite closed-mouth smile that looks slightly uncertain. Black hair pulled back in a low plait, with a few loose strands at the front. Small gold stud earrings and a thin red-and-gold thread on her right wrist, just visible at the bottom of the frame. No glasses. She wears a plain teal cotton kurti with small white embroidery at the neckline and a navy cardigan over it. Behind her is a cream-painted wall with a wall calendar from a local Indian grocer showing a picture of Krishna, a white shelf holding a folded stack of fabric pieces, a clear plastic box of thread spools, and a covered sewing machine. Part of a window frame with a net curtain and a potted tulsi plant shows at the left edge of the image.
